objective: Can two explicit Boolean systems have the same entire family of constrained triples of open choices, with seven allowed states apiece, while their completion questions admit an elementary algorithm on one family and encode all of strict 3-SAT on the other? How many choices suffice to read the relative signs?
status: Complete: A fixed ternary overlap pattern supports both tractable and NP-complete pinned decision families. A separate explicit subfamily has exponentially many non-affine obstructions and precisely linear worst-case decision work.
title: The same overlapping ternary knots with different SAT decisions
